title: 蜘蛛の糸
author: 芥川龍之介
blurb: The Buddha lowers a spider thread to a thief in hell. A short children's story about greed.
note: Published in 1918 and the author died in 1927, so it is in the US public domain (published before 1931).
coverCredit: Kawanabe Kyōsai, Hell Courtesan (Jigoku-dayū), about 1874. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: 杜子春
author: 芥川龍之介
blurb: A young man in old Luoyang is made rich three times by a hermit, then asked to keep silent through anything to become one himself.
note: Published in 1920 in the children's magazine Akai Tori, and the author died in 1927, so it is in the US public domain (published before 1931).
coverCredit: Kanō Sansetsu, the Daoist immortals Li Tieguai and Han Xiangzi, from a set of screens, 17th century. Minneapolis Institute of Art. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: 注文の多い料理店
author: 宮沢賢治
blurb: Two hunters walk into a restaurant in the mountains where the rules keep getting stranger.
note: Published in 1924 in the book of the same name, so it is in the US public domain (published before 1931).
coverCredit: Utagawa Kuniyoshi, cats in many poses, 1852. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: 一房の葡萄
author: 有島武郎
blurb: A shy boy at a foreign school in Yokohama steals a classmate's paints. A kind teacher and a bunch of grapes help him set it right.
note: Published in 1920 in the children's magazine Akai Tori, and the author died in 1923, so it is in the US public domain (published before 1931).
coverCredit: Juan Fernández el Labrador, Still Life with Four Bunches of Grapes, 1630s. Museo del Prado, Madrid. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: 羅生門
author: 芥川龍之介
blurb: A servant waits out the rain under the ruined Rashomon gate in Kyoto and has to decide how to survive.
note: Published in 1915 and the author died in 1927, so it is in the US public domain (published before 1931).
coverCredit: Utagawa Kuniyoshi, Watanabe no Tsuna Fighting the Demon at Rashōmon, 1840s. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: 夢十夜
author: 夏目漱石
blurb: Ten short dreams, each strange and quiet. Most are only a page or two.
note: Published in 1908 and the author died in 1916, so it is in the US public domain (published before 1931).
coverCredit: Tsukioka Yoshitoshi, Chang’e Fleeing to the Moon, from One Hundred Aspects of the Moon, about 1885. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: 坊っちゃん
author: 夏目漱石
blurb: A hot-headed Tokyo teacher is sent to a school in the countryside and makes trouble for everyone, himself included.
note: Published in 1906 and the author died in 1916, so it is in the US public domain (published before 1931).
coverCredit: Utagawa Yoshitora, Steam Railroad in Tokyo, 1871. Honolulu Museum of Art. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: 高瀬舟
author: 森鷗外
blurb: A constable on the night boat out of Kyoto takes a prisoner into exile and wonders why the man looks so content.
note: Published in 1916 in the magazine Chūō Kōron, and the author died in 1922, so it is in the US public domain (published before 1931).
coverCredit: Utagawa Hiroshige, The Yodo River, from Famous Places in Kyoto, 1830s. Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: こころ
author: 夏目漱石
blurb: A student befriends an older man he calls Sensei and slowly learns what Sensei has hidden for years.
note: Published in 1914 and the author died in 1916, so it is in the US public domain (published before 1931).
coverCredit: Kobayashi Kiyochika, The Sumida River at Night, 1881. Honolulu Museum of Art. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: 吾輩は猫である
author: 夏目漱石
blurb: A cat with no name watches his owner, a schoolteacher, and the odd visitors who come to the house.
note: Published in 1905 to 1906 and the author died in 1916, so it is in the US public domain (published before 1931).
coverCredit: Hishida Shunsō, Black Cat, 1910. Eisei Bunko Museum. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: 高野聖
author: 泉鏡花
blurb: A traveling monk tells of a mountain crossing one summer: a snake on the path, a forest of leeches, and a lovely woman in a lonely house.
note: Published in 1900 in the magazine Shin Shōsetsu, and the author died in 1939, so it is in the US public domain (published before 1931).
coverCredit: Katsushika Hokusai, The Amida Falls in the Far Reaches of the Kisokaidō Road, from A Tour of Waterfalls in Various Provinces, about 1827. Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: 雁
author: 森鷗外
blurb: Tokyo, 1880. A moneylender's kept woman falls quietly for a medical student who walks past her house every evening.
note: Published in the magazine Subaru from 1911 to 1913 and as a book in 1915, and the author died in 1922, so it is in the US public domain (published before 1931).
coverCredit: Utagawa Hiroshige, Wild Geese Flying under the Full Moon, about 1833. Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.
